bands.label: Excellent — High Effort Student
bands.text: You're putting in serious effort with smart strategies. Your consistency, active techniques, and exam preparation are at a high level. Keep optimizing — you're on the path to mastery.

bands.label: Good — Solid Effort with Room to Grow
bands.text: You have good habits forming but there are clear gaps. Look at your weakest domain below — even small improvements there will significantly boost your results. You're closer to excellence than you think.

bands.label: Average — Needs Improvement
bands.text: Your effort level is average. You likely know you could do better. The gap between where you are and where you want to be is closable — but it requires changing specific habits, not just 'trying harder'. Focus on the domains marked red/orange below.

bands.label: Low — Significant Change Needed
bands.text: Your current study effort is significantly below what's needed for strong results. This isn't about intelligence — it's about habits and systems. Start with ONE change: set a specific 1-hour study block at the same time every day. Build from there.

Time & Consistency.low: You're spending very little focused time on studies. Consistency is the foundation — even 1 focused hour daily is better than 5 scattered hours before exams.
Time & Consistency.moderate: You're putting in some effort but it's inconsistent. Try building a small daily habit first (even 45 min focused) and grow from there.
Time & Consistency.high: You're investing consistent time and showing discipline. You've built a solid routine — keep refining it.

Techniques & Methods.low: You're relying on passive methods (just reading). Active techniques like self-testing, mind maps, and teaching others are 3-5x more effective.
Techniques & Methods.moderate: You use some good techniques but haven't fully committed to active learning. Try replacing re-reading with recall practice for one week and notice the difference.
Techniques & Methods.high: You're using evidence-based study methods. Active recall, spaced repetition, and varied techniques give you a strong learning advantage.

Revision & Retention.low: Without revision, you forget 80% within a week. The forgetting curve is real. Even 10 minutes of daily review can transform your retention.
Revision & Retention.moderate: You revise but not systematically. Try the 1-3-7-21 rule: revise after 1 day, 3 days, 7 days, and 21 days for permanent memory.
Revision & Retention.high: Your revision system is strong. Regular review and spaced repetition mean you're actually retaining what you learn long-term.

Exam Performance.low: Exam anxiety and blanking out usually means the material wasn't deeply encoded. More practice tests under timed conditions will build exam confidence.
Exam Performance.moderate: You perform okay but feel the pressure. Simulating exam conditions during study (timed, closed book) trains your brain for the real thing.
Exam Performance.high: You perform well under exam pressure. Your preparation strategies — practice papers, time management, and error analysis — are paying off.

Planning & Mindset.low: Without clear goals and self-belief, effort feels directionless. Start by asking 'What exactly will I accomplish in the next hour?' before every session.
Planning & Mindset.moderate: You have some structure but procrastination and self-doubt still hold you back. Small wins build momentum — celebrate tiny progress daily.
Planning & Mindset.high: You have strong planning skills and self-awareness. You know your effort level and continuously work to improve. This mindset is your biggest asset.
